READ-ONLY DIAGNOSIS + PLAN. Do NOT edit or build (other agents run concurrently; one shared _ops.so). Read-only commands fine.

YOUR FAMILY: looksam × {decoder, vit, mamba} (3 cells). wiring_check reports: "MODEL-COUPLED: st.sam_dir needs a SAM 2nd backward in the model phase". LookSAM (sharpness-aware minimization variant) needs a SECOND backward pass: compute gradient g, perturb weights to w+ε·ĝ (ascent step), recompute gradient g_sam there, then use the SAM direction. Currently this 2nd pass isn't coupled into the L3 persistent megakernel's model phase, so the cell runs eager.

1	#pragma once
2	// LookSAM — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Liu et al. 2022, "Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-
5	// Aware Minimization" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02714), Algorithm 1
6	// (periodic-perturbation variant — SAM gradient is recomputed every k
7	// steps, then reused as a cached direction for intervening steps).
8	//
9	// AdamW with periodic Sharpness-Aware Minimization (every k steps).
10	//
11	// Four operations:
12	//   (1) perturb:           p_pert = p + rho * (g / ||g||)
13	//   (2) restore:           p = p_pert - rho * (g / ||g||)
14	//   (3) direction adjust:  on SAM step,    sam_dir = g_sam - g
15	//                          on normal step, g_adj   = (1-alpha)*g + alpha*sam_dir
16	//   (4) standard AdamW update with g_adj.
17	//
18	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
19	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
20	
21	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
22	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
23	
24	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
25	
26	// Step (1) — perturb in gradient direction by rho / ||g||.
27	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
28	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_perturb_step(
29	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
30	    ParamT* __restrict__ backup,
31	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
32	    const float scale,        // rho / (||g|| + eps), precomputed
33	    const int64_t idx
34	) {
35	    const ParamT p = param[idx];
36	    backup[idx] = p;
37	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(static_cast<float>(p) + scale * static_cast<float>(grad[idx]));
38	}
39	
40	// Step (2) — restore parameters from backup.
41	template <typename ParamT>
42	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_restore_step(
43	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
44	    const ParamT* __restrict__ backup,
45	    const int64_t idx
46	) {
47	    param[idx] = backup[idx];
48	}
49	
50	// Step (3) on SAM step: cache the gradient difference.
51	template <typename GradT>
52	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_set_direction(
53	    float* __restrict__ sam_dir,
54	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_sam,
55	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_orig,
56	    const int64_t idx
57	) {
58	    sam_dir[idx] = static_cast<float>(grad_sam[idx]) - static_cast<float>(grad_orig[idx]);
59	}
60	
61	// Step (3) on normal step + Step (4): blend cached SAM direction and run Adam.
62	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
63	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_apply_step(
64	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
65	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
66	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
67	    const float* __restrict__ sam_dir,
68	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
69	    const float alpha,         // SAM blend strength
70	    const float lr,
71	    const float beta1,
72	    const float beta2,
73	    const float eps,
74	    const float wd,
75	    const float bc1,
76	    const float bc2,
77	    const int64_t idx
78	) {
79	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
80	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
81	    const float g_adj = (1.0f - alpha) * g + alpha * sam_dir[idx];
82	
83	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_adj;
84	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_adj * g_adj;
85	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
86	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
87	
88	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
89	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
90	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
91	}
92	
93	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

2	
3	**Scope.** This spec tells the binding/cell/codegen layer how to drive the
4	per-step PRECOMPUTE stages in `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh` so
5	that every optimizer TAIL (`csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::apply_optimizer
6	<OptId>`) can run fully inside one persistent megakernel. It is a wiring
7	contract, not code: it does not touch `opt_components.cuh`,
8	`megakernel_codegen.py`, `dispatch.cpp`, `bindings.cpp`, or any
9	`supergrok2*`/`neuralgrok.py`/`grokadamw.py`/model-stage file (sibling-owned).
10	
11	Today only AdamW / Lion have a complete in-kernel tail (no precompute). The 9
12	non-trivial optimizers are classified below; the 4 STAGED ones get an upstream
13	stage that fills the `FusedOptState` fields their apply reads.
14

18

173	//  space for the eliminated 223 MB grad partials, so it is free real estate.
174	//  Reinterpreted as __nv_bfloat16. Total 80,546,592 bf16 (161 MB) << the 223 MB

180	struct DecActs {
181	    // Per-layer linear INPUTS X (needed by dW = dY^T @ X):
182	    __nv_bfloat16* X_in[dec::kLayers];    // [T, d]    in_proj input (= layer input)
183	    __nv_bfloat16* X_ctx[dec::kLayers];   // [T, d]    out_proj input (attn context)
184	    __nv_bfloat16* X_x1[dec::kLayers];    // [T, d]    ff0 input (n1 output)
185	    __nv_bfloat16* X_gact[dec::kLayers];  // [T, dff]  ff2 input (gelu output)
186	    // Per-layer linear OUTPUT adjoints dY (needed by dW + bias db = Σ_t dY):
187	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_qkv[dec::kLayers];  // [T, 3d]   in_proj output adjoint
188	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_a[dec::kLayers];    // [T, d]    out_proj output adjoint
189	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_ff0[dec::kLayers];  // [T, dff]  ff0 output adjoint
190	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_ff2[dec::kLayers];  // [T, d]    ff2 output adjoint
191	    // Head (B rows — last position only):
192	    __nv_bfloat16* X_hn;                  // [B, d]    head input
193	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_logits;             // [B, V]    head output adjoint (dlogits)
194	    // Embedding-input adjoint (needed by tok/pos owner-scan):
195	    __nv_bfloat16* dh0;                   // [T, d]
196	};

198	__device__ __forceinline__ DecActs dec_acts_bind(__nv_bfloat16* p, int T, int B) {
199	    DecActs a;
200	    int64_t off = 0;
201	    const int64_t Td = (int64_t)T * dec::kD;
202	    const int64_t T3d = (int64_t)T * 3 * dec::kD;
203	    const int64_t Tff = (int64_t)T * dec::kDff;
204	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) {
205	        a.X_in[li]   = p + off; off += Td;
206	        a.X_ctx[li]  = p + off; off += Td;
207	        a.X_x1[li]   = p + off; off += Td;
208	        a.X_gact[li] = p + off; off += Tff;
209	        a.dY_qkv[li] = p + off; off += T3d;
210	        a.dY_a[li]   = p + off; off += Td;
211	        a.dY_ff0[li] = p + off; off += Tff;
212	        a.dY_ff2[li] = p + off; off += Td;
213	    }
214	    a.X_hn      = p + off; off += (int64_t)B * dec::kD;
215	    a.dY_logits = p + off; off += (int64_t)B * dec::kVocab;
216	    a.dh0       = p + off; off += Td;
217	    return a;
218	}

221	//  Canonical Major-K smem stager. The ss-wgmma operand smem tile (MN rows x
222	//  K=16 bf16) MUST be in the CUTLASS Major-K INTERLEAVE layout (wgmma.cuh):
223	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
224	//  This helper writes ONE such MN x 16 tile, pulling element (mn, k) from a
225	//  caller-provided accessor `src(mn, kbase + k)`. Routing the source axis
226	//  through the accessor is what lets the SAME wgmma issue (TransA=0/TransB=0,
227	//  the substrate-validated orientation) serve fwd / dX / dW: the staging loop
228	//  transposes physically; the engine never leaves the gated path.
229	//
230	//  Cooperative over `nthreads` threads starting at thread `t0` (a warpgroup).
231	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
232	template <int MN, typename Src>
233	__device__ __forceinline__ void stage_kmajor_tile(
234	        __nv_bfloat16* smem_tile, int kbase, Src src, int t0, int nthreads) {
235	    // MN*16 elements, each thread strides.
236	    #pragma unroll 1
237	    for (int i = t0; i < MN * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK; i += nthreads) {
238	        const int mn = i / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
239	        const int k  = i % wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
240	        const int dst = (k >> 3) * (MN * 8) + mn * 8 + (k & 7);
241	        smem_tile[dst] = src(mn, kbase + k);
242	    }
243	}

245	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
246	//  Unpipelined single-CTA batch GEMM: D[M,N] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k], bf16 operands
247	//  (accessor-sourced + Major-K staged), fp32 accumulator, ascending-k. M is
248	//  kTileM (kAtomsM stacked m64 atoms — the substrate's unexercised TILE_M
249	//  stacking, gated here). N is a compile-time wgmma atom width. K=k_steps*16.
250	//
251	//  The consumer warpgroup (the FULL CTA's 256 threads act as producer+consumer
252	//  here in the SIMPLE unpipelined form: all 256 stage, then warpgroup 0's 128
253	//  threads — actually wgmma is warpgroup-scoped (.aligned, 128 threads). We use
254	//  ONE warpgroup (threads 0..127) for the MMA; staging uses all 256 threads.
255	//
256	//  smem: one A tile (64x16) + one B tile (Nx16) per stacked atom row, reused
257	//  across k-steps (unpipelined: stage k, mma k, repeat). Two buffers (A,B) of
258	//  the largest atom. Accumulators live in registers (kAtomsM fragments).
259	//
260	//  ACC OUTPUT: written via accessor `out(m_global, n_local, value)` so the
261	//  caller routes the fp32 result (the fragment decode gives (row,col) within the
262	//  64xN atom; the caller adds the atom's M-base).
263	//
264	//  GENERALITY (the M and N must be caller-parameterized, NOT hardwired to the
265	//  token tile — a dW GEMM has M = Nout in {99,128,384,512} and the fwd GEMMs
266	//  have N in {128,384,512}). This helper computes ONE M-block of `m_atoms`
267	//  stacked m64 atoms (rows [mbase0, mbase0 + m_atoms*64)) for ONE N-tile of the
268	//  compile-time atom width N. The CALLER loops M-atom-blocks × N-tiles to cover
269	//  arbitrary (M, N). MaxAtomsM bounds the register accumulator array
270	//  (compile-time); only `m_atoms` (<= MaxAtomsM) atoms are issued at runtime.
271	//  `n_real <= N` lets the caller mark the valid column count for a ragged N-tile
272	//  (e.g. head V=99 in a N=128 tile) so the epilogue suppresses pad columns; the
273	//  wgmma still runs the full N (pad operands are zero so pad outputs are inert).
274	//
275	//  Determinism: ascending-k, one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, no atomics.
276	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
277	template <int N, int MaxAtomsM, typename SrcA, typename SrcB, typename Out>
278	__device__ void tc_gemm_block_unpipelined(
279	        int mbase0, int m_atoms, int n_real, int k_steps,
280	        SrcA srcA, SrcB srcB, Out out,
281	        __nv_bfloat16* smemA, __nv_bfloat16* smemB) {
282	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
283	    const int tid = threadIdx.x;
284	    const int nthreads = blockDim.x;            // 256
285	    const bool in_wg0 = (tid < 128);
286	    const int tid_wg = tid & 127;
287	
288	    // One fp32 accumulator fragment per stacked m64 atom (compile-time bound).
289	    wgs::WgmmaAccum<N> acc[MaxAtomsM];
290	    constexpr int S = kDecTcStages;
291	
292	    // Stage tile `k` of atom `mbase` into ring slot `k % S` (smem{A,B} are ring bases).
293	    auto stage_k = [&] (int mbase, int k) {
294	        const int sl = k % S;
295	        stage_kmajor_tile<wgs::kWgmmaAtomM>(
296	            smemA + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemA1, k * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK,
297	            [&] (int mn, int kk) { return srcA(mbase + mn, kk); }, tid, nthreads);
298	        stage_kmajor_tile<N>(
299	            smemB + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemB1, k * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK,
300	            [&] (int mn, int kk) { return srcB(mn, kk); }, tid, nthreads);
301	    };
302	    auto issue_k = [&] (int a, int k) {
303	        const int sl = k % S;
304	        wgs::SmemDesc dA = wgs::make_desc_A_kmajor<wgs::kWgmmaAtomM, wgs::kSwizzleNone>(
305	            smemA + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemA1);
306	        wgs::SmemDesc dB = wgs::make_desc_B_kmajor<N, wgs::kSwizzleNone>(
307	            smemB + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemB1);
308	        if (k == 0) wgs::wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, 0, 0>(acc[a], dA, dB);
309	        else        wgs::wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, 0, 0>(acc[a], dA, dB);
310	    };
311	
312	    // For each stacked atom (M-base = mbase0 + a*64), run the full k-chain.
313	    #pragma unroll 1
314	    for (int a = 0; a < m_atoms; ++a) {
315	        const int mbase = mbase0 + a * wgs::kWgmmaAtomM;
316	        // Prologue: stage tile 0; make visible; fence.
317	        stage_k(mbase, 0);
318	        __syncthreads();
319	        if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_fence();
320	        // Steady state (S=2 single-in-flight double-buffer): issue wgmma(k) on the
321	        // already-staged slot k&1 (async), THEN stage tile k+1 into the OTHER slot
322	        // (its HBM loads overlap the MMA), THEN wait_group<0> + sync (wgmma(k) done
323	        // reading slot k&1; stage(k+1) visible; slot k&1 reuse-safe). S=1 collapses
324	        // to the validated serial path (stage k+1 into the single slot AFTER wait).
325	        #pragma unroll 1
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            if (in_wg0) { issue_k(a, k); wgs::wgmma_commit_group(); }
328	            if (S > 1) {
329	                if (k + 1 < k_steps) stage_k(mbase, k + 1);
330	                if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_wait_group<0>();
331	                __syncthreads();
332	            } else {
333	                if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_wait_group<0>();
334	                __syncthreads();
335	                if (k + 1 < k_steps) { stage_k(mbase, k + 1); __syncthreads(); }
336	            }
337	        }
338	        // Epilogue: warpgroup 0 owns the fp32 fragment; decode + emit (real cols).
339	        if (in_wg0) {
340	            #pragma unroll
341	            for (int i = 0; i < wgs::WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
342	                int row, col;
343	                wgs::wgmma_frag_decode(tid_wg, i, N, row, col);
344	                if (col < n_real) out(mbase + row, col, acc[a].c[i]);
345	            }
346	        }
347	        __syncthreads();
348	    }
349	#else
350	    (void)mbase0; (void)m_atoms; (void)n_real; (void)k_steps;
351	    (void)srcA; (void)srcB; (void)out; (void)smemA; (void)smemB;
352	#endif
353	}

356	//  THIN ORIENTATION WRAPPERS over tc_gemm_block_unpipelined. These reproduce
357	//  the THREE accessor patterns the engine is silicon-validated on
358	//  (decoder_tc_selftest.cu / test_decoder_tc.py 13/13): fwd (Y=X·Wᵀ, no
359	//  transpose), dX (dX=dY·W, W transposed-staged), dW (dW=dYᵀ·X, BOTH
360	//  transposed-staged, K=T). The driver calls THESE — it never re-derives the
361	//  staging (the no-suppression / reuse-the-validated-unit discipline).
362	//
363	//  All operands are HBM bf16 row-major. The caller passes one A(64×16) + one
364	//  B(Nmax×16) smem staging pair (the engine reuses them across k-steps). N is
365	//  the compile-time wgmma atom width (128 for in/out/ff dX-N=d; the fwd loops
366	//  N-tiles internally). Accumulation is fp32; output written via the accessor.
367	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
368	
369	// (fwd) Y[M,Nout] = X[M,Kin] @ W[Nout,Kin]ᵀ.  Tiles N over [0,Nout) in width-N
370	// atoms (Nout∈{d=128, 3d=384, dff=512}). M = kTileM (kAtomsM stacked atoms).
371	// Y is written row-major [M, Nout] at base `Yout` with row stride Nout.
372	// NOTE on weights: the params blob is fp32; the wgmma engine needs bf16 B
373	// operands. We convert ON READ in the accessor (`__float2bfloat16(W[...])`) —
374	// deterministic, so every read yields the same bf16 (determinism-safe), and it
375	// needs NO bf16 weight buffer or cross-CTA conversion phase. Cost: weight bytes
376	// read as fp32 (2×) in fwd/dX — a perf-phase optimization, not a correctness gate.
377	template <int N>

437	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
438	//  Per-CTA TILE SCRATCH (HBM). One tile's forward intermediates the backward
439	//  reads, reused across the tiles a CTA grid-strides over (a CTA finishes a
440	//  tile's fwd+bwd before the next tile, so one slab per CTA suffices). Sized
441	//  for kTileM rows. The X-inputs / dY-adjoints that OTHER CTAs read in P2's dW
442	//  do NOT live here — they live in the full-T DecActs (cross-CTA). This holds
443	//  only the within-tile fwd state + the running adjoint so the backward needs
444	//  NO recompute.
445	//
446	//  DEDICATED, NON-ALIASED buffers (the TC test sizes its own workspace; HBM is
447	//  NOT scarce, so hand-managed aliasing — the stride/alias bug class that bit
448	//  the scalar path at model_stages_decoder.cuh:619-625, which the CPU mirror
449	//  does NOT cover for tile-batched reuse — is avoided entirely). Each fp32
450	//  intermediate gets its own slot.
451	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
452	
453	// nSamp samples per tile, H*S*S attention entries each; V logits each.
454	constexpr int kNSampPerTile  = kTileM / dec::kSeq;
455	constexpr int kAttnPerTile   = kNSampPerTile * dec::kHeads * dec::kSeq * dec::kSeq;
456	constexpr int kLogitsPerTile = kNSampPerTile * dec::kVocab;
457	
458	// CRITICAL: the forward runs ALL layers, THEN the backward runs ALL layers (NOT
459	// interleaved per-layer). So every forward intermediate the backward reads PER
460	// LAYER must be stored PER LAYER — a single-buffered cache holds only the LAST
461	// layer's values and the earlier layers' backward reads garbage (the "forward
462	// exact, layer-0 grads wrong, error compounds backward" bug). qkv / ff0pre /
463	// attn / n1·n2 LN caches are therefore [kLayers]-indexed. fnx/fni (final norm,
464	// one instance) + the transient dh/x1/finalin/logits/work/work2/dsc stay single.
465	struct DecTileScratch {
466	    __nv_bfloat16* qkv[dec::kLayers];     // [kTileM, 3d]  per layer
467	    __nv_bfloat16* ff0pre[dec::kLayers];  // [kTileM, dff] per layer
468	    float* attn[dec::kLayers];            // [kAttnPerTile] per layer
469	    float* n1x[dec::kLayers]; float* n1i[dec::kLayers];
470	    float* n2x[dec::kLayers]; float* n2i[dec::kLayers];
471	    float* dsc;             // [kAttnPerTile] attention dscores (transient, bwd-only)
472	    float* fnx; float* fni; // final-norm LN caches (single)
473	    float* dh;              // [kTileM, d]    running adjoint wrt block output
474	    float* x1;              // [kTileM, d]    n1 output (fp32, residual base for r2)
475	    float* finalin;         // [kTileM, d]    last-layer n2 output (fp32, head input)
476	    float* logits;          // [kLogitsPerTile] per-sample last-pos logits (fp32)
477	    float* work;            // [kTileM, dff]  GEMM output / general fp32 scratch
478	    float* work2;           // [kTileM, dff]  second fp32 scratch (bwd dx1/dqkv)
479	};

481	// Bytes one CTA's scratch occupies (for host sizing of the workspace tail).
482	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tile_scratch_bf16_count() {
483	    // (qkv + ff0pre) per layer.
484	    return (int64_t)dec::kLayers * ((int64_t)kTileM * 3 * dec::kD + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff);
485	}
486	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tile_scratch_f32_count() {
487	    return (int64_t)dec::kLayers * (                     // per-layer:
488	             (int64_t)kAttnPerTile                       //   attn
489	           + 2 * ((int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD + kTileM))    //   n1+n2 xhat+inv
490	         + (int64_t)kAttnPerTile                          // dsc (single)
491	         + ((int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD + kTileM)           // fn xhat+inv (single)
492	         + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD                      // dh
493	         + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD                      // x1
494	         + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD                      // finalin
495	         + (int64_t)kLogitsPerTile                        // logits
496	         + 2 * (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff;               // work + work2
497	}
498	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tile_scratch_total_f32() {
499	    return (dec_tile_scratch_bf16_count() + 1) / 2 + dec_tile_scratch_f32_count();
500	}

502	__device__ __forceinline__ DecTileScratch dec_tile_scratch_bind(float* slab) {
503	    DecTileScratch s;
504	    __nv_bfloat16* b = reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(slab);
505	    int64_t bo = 0;
506	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.qkv[li]    = b + bo; bo += (int64_t)kTileM * 3 * dec::kD; }
507	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.ff0pre[li] = b + bo; bo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff; }
508	    float* f = slab + (dec_tile_scratch_bf16_count() + 1) / 2;
509	    int64_t fo = 0;
510	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.attn[li] = f + fo; fo += kAttnPerTile; }
511	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.n1x[li] = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD; s.n1i[li] = f + fo; fo += kTileM; }
512	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.n2x[li] = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD; s.n2i[li] = f + fo; fo += kTileM; }
513	    s.dsc  = f + fo; fo += kAttnPerTile;
514	    s.fnx  = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
515	    s.fni  = f + fo; fo += kTileM;
516	    s.dh   = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
517	    s.x1   = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
518	    s.finalin = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
519	    s.logits  = f + fo; fo += kLogitsPerTile;
520	    s.work    = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff;
521	    s.work2   = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff;
522	    return s;
523	}

526	//  TILE-AWARE SCALAR ELEMENTWISE STAGES (fp32, CTA-cooperative over kTileM
527	//  rows). These mirror the scalar oracle's per-row math (model_stages_decoder
528	//  .cuh) but operate on a whole tile of `nrows` rows at once, reading/writing
529	//  HBM [rows×width] buffers. Reductions reuse the validated dec_block_sum /
530	//  dec_block_max helpers (whole-block, looped per row — LN/softmax are ≪1% of
531	//  FLOPs, so the sequential row loop is not a bottleneck). `red` is a 256-float
532	//  smem reduction slot (from the engine's smem arena).
533	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
534	
535	// LayerNorm fwd over the last dim d, for `nrows` rows. y, xhat are fp32 HBM
536	// [rows×d]; inv is fp32 HBM [rows]. gamma/beta are fp32 [d] (params). Caches
537	// xhat+inv for the bwd (identical to dec_layernorm_fwd but tiled).
538	__device__ __forceinline__ void dectc_ln_fwd_tile(
539	        const float* __restrict__ x, const float* __restrict__ gamma,
540	        const float* __restrict__ beta, int nrows,
541	        float* __restrict__ y, float* __restrict__ xhat, float* __restrict__ inv,
542	        float* red) {
543	    for (int s = 0; s < nrows; ++s) {
544	        const float* xr = x + (int64_t)s * dec::kD;
545	        float sum = 0.0f;
546	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < dec::kD; j += blockDim.x) sum += xr[j];
547	        float mean = dec_block_sum(sum, red) / (float)dec::kD;
548	        float vs = 0.0f;
549	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < dec::kD; j += blockDim.x) { float c = xr[j] - mean; vs += c * c; }
550	        float var = dec_block_sum(vs, red) / (float)dec::kD;
551	        float iv = rsqrtf(var + dec::kLnEps);
552	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) inv[s] = iv;
553	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < dec::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
554	            float xh = (xr[j] - mean) * iv;
555	            xhat[(int64_t)s * dec::kD + j] = xh;
556	            y[(int64_t)s * dec::kD + j] = xh * gamma[j] + beta[j];
557	        }
558	        __syncthreads();
559	    }
560	}

562	// LayerNorm bwd for `nrows` rows: dy [rows×d] fp32, cached xhat/inv → dx [rows×d]
563	// fp32; ACCUMULATES dgamma/dbeta (summed over the tile's rows) into a per-CTA
564	// LN-vec partial slot gw/gb [d] (plain += : single owner thread per feature j
565	// across rows, deterministic — same rule as the scalar dec_layernorm_bwd).
566	__device__ __forceinline__ void dectc_ln_bwd_tile(
567	        const float* __restrict__ dy, const float* __restrict__ xhat,
568	        const float* __restrict__ inv, const float* __restrict__ gamma, int nrows,
569	        float* __restrict__ dx, float* __restrict__ gw, float* __restrict__ gb,
570	        float* red) {
571	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < dec::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
572	        float dgw = 0.0f, dgb = 0.0f;
573	        for (int s = 0; s < nrows; ++s) {
574	            float d = dy[(int64_t)s * dec::kD + j];
575	            dgb += d; dgw += d * xhat[(int64_t)s * dec::kD + j];
576	        }
577	        gw[j] += dgw; gb[j] += dgb;
578	    }
579	    for (int s = 0; s < nrows; ++s) {
580	        const float* dyr = dy + (int64_t)s * dec::kD;
581	        const float* xhr = xhat + (int64_t)s * dec::kD;
582	        float sda = 0.0f, sdax = 0.0f;
583	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < dec::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
584	            float dxhat = dyr[j] * gamma[j]; sda += dxhat; sdax += dxhat * xhr[j];
585	        }
586	        sda = dec_block_sum(sda, red);
587	        sdax = dec_block_sum(sdax, red);
588	        float iv = inv[s];
589	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < dec::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
590	            float dxhat = dyr[j] * gamma[j];
591	            dx[(int64_t)s * dec::kD + j] = iv * (dxhat - (sda + xhr[j] * sdax) / (float)dec::kD);
592	        }
593	        __syncthreads();
594	    }
595	}

597	// Per-sample causal self-attention FORWARD over a tile. qkv is bf16 HBM
598	// [rows×3d] (q|k|v). Writes ctx fp32 HBM [rows×d] and attn weights fp32 to
599	// `attn_w` [nSamp×H×S×S]. Each (sample,head,qpos) row is owned by one thread —
600	// identical math to dec_forward_sample's attention block, looped over samples.
601	__device__ __forceinline__ void dectc_attn_fwd_tile(
602	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ qkv, int nrows,
603	        float* __restrict__ ctx, float* __restrict__ attn_w) {
604	    const int nsamp = nrows / dec::kSeq;
605	    const float scale = dec::attn_scale();
606	    const int rows_per = nsamp * dec::kHeads * dec::kSeq;   // (sample,head,qpos)
607	    for (int r = threadIdx.x; r < rows_per; r += blockDim.x) {
608	        const int si = r / (dec::kHeads * dec::kSeq);
609	        const int rem = r % (dec::kHeads * dec::kSeq);
610	        const int hh = rem / dec::kSeq, qi = rem % dec::kSeq;
611	        const int qoff = hh * dec::kDhead;
612	        const int rbase = si * dec::kSeq;        // first row of this sample
613	        const __nv_bfloat16* qrow = qkv + (int64_t)(rbase + qi) * 3 * dec::kD + qoff;
614	        float maxs = -CUDART_INF_F; float sc[dec::kSeq];
615	        #pragma unroll
616	        for (int kj = 0; kj < dec::kSeq; ++kj) {
617	            if (kj > qi) { sc[kj] = -CUDART_INF_F; continue; }
618	            const __nv_bfloat16* krow = qkv + (int64_t)(rbase + kj) * 3 * dec::kD + dec::kD + qoff;
619	            float dot = 0.0f;
620	            #pragma unroll
621	            for (int t = 0; t < dec::kDhead; ++t)
622	                dot += __bfloat162float(qrow[t]) * __bfloat162float(krow[t]);
623	            sc[kj] = dot * scale; maxs = fmaxf(maxs, sc[kj]);
624	        }
625	        float denom = 0.0f;
626	        #pragma unroll
627	        for (int kj = 0; kj < dec::kSeq; ++kj) {
628	            float e = (kj <= qi) ? __expf(sc[kj] - maxs) : 0.0f; sc[kj] = e; denom += e;
629	        }
630	        float invd = 1.0f / denom;
631	        float* aw = attn_w + ((int64_t)(si * dec::kHeads + hh) * dec::kSeq + qi) * dec::kSeq;
632	        #pragma unroll
633	        for (int kj = 0; kj < dec::kSeq; ++kj) aw[kj] = sc[kj] * invd;
634	        #pragma unroll
635	        for (int t = 0; t < dec::kDhead; ++t) {
636	            float acc = 0.0f;
637	            #pragma unroll
638	            for (int kj = 0; kj <= qi; ++kj) {
639	                float vv = __bfloat162float(qkv[(int64_t)(rbase + kj) * 3 * dec::kD + 2 * dec::kD + qoff + t]);
640	                acc += aw[kj] * vv;
641	            }
642	            ctx[(int64_t)(rbase + qi) * dec::kD + qoff + t] = acc;
643	        }
644	    }
645	    __syncthreads();
646	}

651	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
652	//  FORWARD over one TOKEN TILE (nrows = nsamp samples × kSeq positions), global
653	//  token rows [g0, g0+nrows). Tile-batched: the four per-layer linears
654	//  (in_proj/out_proj/ff0/ff2) run on wgmma (M=nrows, N-tiled); attention/LN/
655	//  GELU are scalar fp32 over the tile; head/CE are scalar per-sample (M=nsamp<
656	//  64). Writes the DecActs X-inputs (bf16 dW operands), the per-CTA tile scratch
657	//  (qkv/ff0pre/attn/LN caches/x1/finalin/logits the bwd needs), and returns the
658	//  tile's summed NLL (thread 0 holds it). `tok_ids`/`tgt_ids` are HBM int32.
659	//
660	//  DATAFLOW (DecActs X-regions = bf16 dW operands AND inter-stage operands;
661	//  dedicated fp32 scratch for residuals/LN; weights convert fp32→bf16 on read):
662	//    X_in[li]  := layer input (bf16)           [embedding for li=0]
663	//    qkv(bf16) := X_in @ in_w^T + in_b   (in_b folded fp32 → re-round bf16)
664	//    ctx       := attn(qkv) → X_ctx[li] (bf16, out_proj input + dW operand)
665	//    a(work)   := X_ctx @ out_w^T ; r1=X_in+a+out_b (work); n1(r1)→x1(fp32)→X_x1[li]
666	//    ff0(work) := X_x1 @ ff0_w^T ; (ff0+ff0_b)→ff0pre(bf16); gelu(ff0+ff0_b)→X_gact[li](bf16)
667	//    ff2(work) := X_gact @ ff2_w^T ; r2=x1+ff2+ff2_b (work); n2(r2)→X_in[li+1]
668	//                 (last layer: n2→finalin fp32, the head input)
669	//  BIASES (in/out/ff0/ff2) are folded in fp32 at these points (the oracle adds
670	//  them in fp32 after the bf16 matmul); LN β + head out_b were already applied.
671	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
672	__device__ float dectc_forward_tile(
673	        const DecWeights& w, int g0, int nrows, const DecActs& acts,
674	        const DecTileScratch& sc, const int* __restrict__ tok_ids,
675	        const int* __restrict__ tgt_ids,
676	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB, float* red) {
677	    const int nsamp = nrows / dec::kSeq;
678	    // ── Embedding: X_in[0][r] = tok[token_id[g0+r]] + pos[(g0+r)%S]. bf16. ──
679	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * dec::kD; idx += blockDim.x) {
680	        const int r = idx / dec::kD, j = idx % dec::kD;
681	        const int g = g0 + r;
682	        const int tid = tok_ids[g];
683	        const int sp = g % dec::kSeq;            // position within the sample
684	        float v = w.tok[(int64_t)tid * dec::kD + j] + w.pos[(int64_t)sp * dec::kD + j];
685	        acts.X_in[0][(int64_t)g * dec::kD + j] = __float2bfloat16(v);
686	    }
687	    __syncthreads();
688	
689	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) {
690	        const DecWeights::Layer& L = w.layer[li];
691	        const __nv_bfloat16* Xin = acts.X_in[li] + (int64_t)g0 * dec::kD;        // [nrows,d]
692	        // qkv = Xin @ in_w^T + in_b   (N=3d, K=d). bf16 → scratch.qkv[li].
693	        dectc_gemm_fwd<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(Xin, L.in_w, sc.qkv[li], dec::kD, 3 * dec::kD, sA, sB);
694	        __syncthreads();
695	        // add in_b (the fwd GEMM did W only; bias folded in scalar here for qkv —
696	        // matches the bf16-faithful oracle qkv = bf(x_in @ bf(in_w)^T + in_b)).
697	        for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * 3 * dec::kD; idx += blockDim.x) {
698	            const int j = idx % (3 * dec::kD);
699	            float v = __bfloat162float(sc.qkv[li][idx]) + L.in_b[j];
700	            sc.qkv[li][idx] = __float2bfloat16(v);
701	        }

25	    """AdamW with sharpness-aware direction adjustment (LookSAM).
26	
27	    The standard ``step()`` performs a regular AdamW update. Sharpness-aware
28	    perturbation and gradient direction adjustment are handled separately via
29	    :meth:`sam_step`, which should be called periodically (every *k* steps)
30	    by the training loop.
31	
32	    Args:
33	        params: Iterable of parameters or parameter groups.
34	        lr: Learning rate (default: 1e-3).
35	        betas: Coefficients for running averages of gradient and its
36	            square (default: (0.9, 0.98)).

38	        weight_decay: Decoupled weight decay coefficient (default: 1.0).
39	        rho: SAM perturbation radius (default: 0.05).

41	            every *k* steps (default: 5).
42	        alpha: Direction adjustment interpolation weight (default: 0.7).
43	    """
44	
45	    def __init__(
46	        self,
47	        params: Iterable,
48	        lr: float = 1e-3,
49	        betas: Tuple[float, float] = (0.9, 0.98),
50	        eps: float = 1e-8,
51	        weight_decay: float = 1.0,
52	        rho: float = 0.05,
53	        k: int = 5,
54	        alpha: float = 0.7,
55	        use_grad_hooks: bool = False,
56	    ) -> None:
57	        if lr < 0.0:
58	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid learning rate: {lr}")
59	        if eps < 0.0:
60	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid epsilon value: {eps}")
61	        if not 0.0 <= betas[0] < 1.0:
62	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid beta parameter at index 0: {betas[0]}")
63	        if not 0.0 <= betas[1] < 1.0:
64	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid beta parameter at index 1: {betas[1]}")
65	        if rho < 0.0:
66	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid rho value: {rho}")
67	        if k < 1:
68	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid k value: {k}")
69	
70	        defaults = dict(
71	            lr=lr,
72	            betas=betas,
73	            eps=eps,
74	            weight_decay=weight_decay,
75	            rho=rho,
76	            k=k,
77	            alpha=alpha,
78	        )
79	        super().__init__(params, defaults)
80	        self._global_step: int = 0
81	
82	        # Per-group cache of static tensor lists (params + exp_avg/exp_avg_sq
83	        # buffers keep a fixed identity across steps); only grads_list and step
84	        # counters are refreshed per step. Invalidated by add_param_group.
85	        self._static_cache: dict = {}
86	        # Lazily-bound fused kernel callable (resolved once at first step()).
87	        self._fused_step = None

90	        if use_grad_hooks:

98	        """Cached (params, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, states) for the AdamW step(),
99	        keyed on the grad-bearing param ids."""
100	        key = tuple(id(p) for p in group["params"] if p.grad is not None)
101	        cached = self._static_cache.get(id(group))
102	        if cached is not None and cached[0] == key:
103	            return cached[1]
104	        params_list = []
105	        exp_avg_list = []
106	        exp_avg_sq_list = []
107	        states = []
108	        for p in group["params"]:
109	            if p.grad is None:
110	                continue
111	            state = self.state[p]
112	            if len(state) == 0:
113	                state["step"] = 0
114	                state["exp_avg"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
115	                state["exp_avg_sq"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
116	                state["sam_direction"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
117	            params_list.append(p)
118	            exp_avg_list.append(state["exp_avg"])
119	            exp_avg_sq_list.append(state["exp_avg_sq"])
120	            states.append(state)

123	        return entry

126	    def step(self, closure=None) -> Optional[float]:
127	        """Perform a standard AdamW optimisation step.
128	
129	        SAM perturbation is **not** applied here; call :meth:`sam_step`
130	        separately when sharpness-aware updates are desired.
131	
132	        Args:
133	            closure: A closure that re-evaluates the model and returns the loss
134	                (optional).
135	
136	        Returns:
137	            The loss value if *closure* is provided, otherwise ``None``.
138	        """
139	        loss = None
140	        if closure is not None:
141	            with torch.enable_grad():
142	                loss = closure()
143	
144	        self._global_step += 1
145	
146	        if self._use_grad_hooks:
147	            return loss
148	
149	        fused_step = self._fused_step
150	        if fused_step is None:
151	            fused_step = self._fused_step = _ops.bind("fused_adamw_simple_step")
152	
153	        for group in self.param_groups:
154	            params_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, states = \
155	                self._group_cache(group)
156	
157	            if len(params_list) == 0:
158	                continue
159	
160	            # Canonical LookSAM ``apply`` (csrc/algorithms/looksam.h
161	            # ``looksam_apply_step``): on EVERY step blend the cached SAM
162	            # direction into the gradient before the AdamW update,
163	            #   g_adj = (1 - alpha) * g + alpha * sam_dir,
164	            # where ``sam_dir`` was cached by the most recent ``sam_step``.
165	            # This is the amortization that makes the k-1 intervening steps
166	            # sharpness-aware. Before the first ``sam_step`` the cached
167	            # direction is zero, so g_adj = (1 - alpha) * g — identical to the
168	            # kernel, which applies the same blend unconditionally.
169	            alpha = group["alpha"]
170	            grads_list = []
171	            step_list = []
172	            for p, state in zip(params_list, states):
173	                sam_dir = state["sam_direction"]
174	                # Validate (sparse/CPU/dtype/contiguity) before the data_ptr is
175	                # handed to the fused kernel — looksam blends the validated grad.
176	                g = _validate_grad(p)
177	                grads_list.append((1.0 - alpha) * g + alpha * sam_dir)
178	                state["step"] += 1
179	                step_list.append(state["step"])
180	
181	            fused_step(
182	                params_list,
183	                grads_list,
184	                exp_avg_list,
185	                exp_avg_sq_list,
186	                step_list,
187	                group["betas"][0],
188	                group["betas"][1],

196	    @torch.no_grad()
197	    def sam_step(
198	        self,
199	        model: torch.nn.Module,
200	        train_x: Tensor,
201	        train_y: Tensor,
202	        criterion: Callable,
203	    ) -> None:
204	        """Perform a LookSAM sharpness-aware gradient direction adjustment.
205	
206	        This method:
207	          1. Saves current gradients and backs up parameters.
208	          2. Perturbs parameters in the sharpness direction.
209	          3. Computes gradients at the perturbed point.
210	          4. Restores original parameters.
211	          5. Computes and stores sharpness-aware directions.
212	          6. Adjusts current gradients using those directions.
213	
214	        Should be called every *k* training steps (see constructor).
215	
216	        Args:
217	            model: The model whose parameters are being optimised.
218	            train_x: Input batch for re-evaluating loss at the perturbed point.
219	            train_y: Target batch.
220	            criterion: Loss function ``criterion(model(train_x), train_y)``.
221	        """
222	        # Collect per-group data in a single pass so it survives across phases
223	        group_data = []
224	        for group in self.param_groups:
225	            params_list = []
226	            orig_grads_list = []
227	            direction_list = []
228	
229	            for p in group["params"]:
230	                if p.grad is None:
231	                    continue
232	                state = self.state[p]
233	                if len(state) == 0:
234	                    state["step"] = 0
235	                    state["exp_avg"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
236	                    state["exp_avg_sq"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
237	                    state["sam_direction"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
238	                params_list.append(p)
239	                orig_grads_list.append(p.grad.clone())
240	                direction_list.append(state["sam_direction"])
241	
242	            if len(params_list) == 0:
243	                group_data.append(None)
244	                continue
245	
246	            # Step 1: Perturb parameters — returns backups
247	            backups = _ops.looksam_perturb_all(
248	                params_list,
249	                orig_grads_list,
250	                group["rho"],
251	            )
252	            group_data.append((params_list, orig_grads_list, direction_list, backups, group))
253	
254	        # Step 2: Forward pass at the perturbed point
255	        model.zero_grad()
256	        with torch.enable_grad():
257	            perturbed_loss = criterion(model(train_x), train_y)
258	            perturbed_loss.backward()
259	
260	        # Step 3 & 4: Restore parameters, then CACHE the SAM direction.
261	        for gd in group_data:
262	            if gd is None:
263	                continue
264	            params_list, orig_grads_list, direction_list, backups, group = gd
265	
266	            # Collect perturbed gradients (∇L at the perturbed point).
267	            perturbed_grads_list = [p.grad.clone() for p in params_list]
268	
269	            # Restore original parameters
270	            _ops.looksam_restore_all(params_list, backups)
271	
272	            # Canonical LookSAM ``set_direction`` (csrc/algorithms/looksam.h:
273	            # ``sam_dir = g_sam - g``): cache the gradient difference into the
274	            # per-parameter ``sam_direction`` state. This is the whole point of
275	            # LookSAM — the direction is REUSED by ``step()`` on the k-1
276	            # intervening (non-SAM) steps via the cached-direction blend. The
277	            # previous code adjusted ``p.grad`` in place for the current step
278	            # only and never wrote ``sam_direction``, so it was dead state and
279	            # every intervening step degenerated to plain AdamW (no SAM at all).
280	            #
281	            # We also restore ``p.grad`` to the ORIGINAL gradient so the
282	            # immediately-following ``step()`` blends from a clean g (matching
283	            # the kernel contract where ``looksam_apply_step`` receives the
284	            # unperturbed grad and the freshly cached direction).
285	            for p, og, pg, sam_dir in zip(
286	                    params_list, orig_grads_list, perturbed_grads_list,
287	                    direction_list):
288	                sam_dir.copy_((pg - og).to(sam_dir.dtype))
289	                p.grad.copy_(og)

310	        sd["_looksam"] = {"_global_step": self._global_step}
311	        return sd

314	        """Restore the SAM-cadence counter, then the base state.
315	
316	        Pops the private ``"_looksam"`` blob (default-absent so OLD checkpoints

318	        """

321	        if blob is not None:
322	            self._global_step = blob.get("_global_step", self._global_step)
323	        super().load_state_dict(sd)

326	        """Per-parameter step used by the `use_grad_hooks=True` path.

339	        # SAM direction every step (g_adj = (1-alpha)*g + alpha*sam_dir) so the
340	        # hooks path is also sharpness-aware on intervening steps, not plain
341	        # AdamW. sam_direction is refreshed by sam_step on the SAM steps.
342	        sam_dir = state.setdefault(

The comment at `:578-580` is explicit: -1 means "an optimizer whose L3-TC path needs more than the fwd+bwd+tail single launch (prodigy/muon/SG11/SG15/**looksam**/SG2)". With -1, `dec_l3_real` (dispatch.cpp:708-710) is false on the wgmma path, so the cell never reaches `launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc` and runs eager. Mirrored on the host in `grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py`: looksam is absent from the `_FUSED_L3_REAL` frozenset (dispatch.py:667-691); `fused_train_step` raises `KeyError` for any cell not in it (dispatch.py:1401-1404).

**(b) The real blocker — the SAM 2nd backward is a whole second model pipeline, and the megakernel provides exactly one.**
The canonical math needs `st.sam_dir = g_sam − g` (`csrc/algorithms/looksam.h:52-59`), where `g_sam` is the gradient evaluated at the **perturbed** weights `p + rho·g/‖g‖` (`looksam.h:27-38`). `looksam_apply_step` (`looksam.h:63-91`, the in-kernel tail via `apply_optimizer<LookSAM>`) reads `st.sam_dir` as a bound input but **cannot produce it** — it is an optimizer tail, not a model stage. INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md §6 (lines 312-327) states this is "the model-stage owner's responsibility," and the `FusedOptState.sam_dir` field already exists as the bound pointer.

The TC megakernel computes the gradient **exactly once**. Concretely in `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`:
- **P1** (`:438-447`): `dectc_forward_tile` → `dectc_backward_tile` per token tile, producing acts (X inputs + dY adjoints) and the loss.
- **B1** barrier (`:449`).
- **P2** (`:456-481`): assembles all 30 grads into the global `grad` buffer (dW output-stationary GEMMs `dectc_dw_run_tile`, biases, `dectc_embed_owner_scan`, `dectc_lnvec_reduce`).
- **B2** `sync_reset` (`:483`).
- Optional opt-specific precompute between B2 and P3 — **P2.5** GrokAdamW clip (`:497`), **P2.6** Prodigy d-reduction (`:557`), **P2.7** Muon Newton-Schulz (`:609`).

There is **no second `g_sam` evaluation** anywhere in this sequence, and `sam_dir` is never written. Critically, the existing precompute stages (P2.5/2.6/2.7) all operate on the **already-reduced grad in `grad`** (element-local, per-tensor reductions, or NS matmuls) — none re-enters the model graph. The SAM perturbation needs `g_sam`, which requires re-running the **entire P1+P2 pipeline** (forward_tile → backward_tile → dW assembly) a second time at perturbed weights. ## (2) Concrete design — SAM 2nd pass inside the persistent kernel

The insertion point is **between B2 and P3** — a new opt-guarded phase `P2.4 (LookSAM ONLY)`, structurally parallel to the existing P2.5/2.6/2.7 `if constexpr (Opt == OptId::…)` blocks. After B2 the reduced first-pass `grad` is live in global and all params are intact; that is exactly the precondition the eager `sam_step` assumes (it clones `p.grad` as `orig_grads`).

Per-model TC megakernel (`fused_{decoder,vit,mamba}_megakernel.cuh`), inside `fused_*_megakernel_tc`, add after the B2 `sync_reset`:

```

  // 0. Compute global ‖g‖ over the reduced grad (deterministic ascending
  //    per-CTA partial → CTA0 owner-sum → broadcast scale = rho/(‖g‖+eps)),
  //    reusing the GrokAdamW P2.5 global-L2 reduction machinery verbatim.
  // 1. PERTURB: p_backup[i]=p[i]; p[i]=p[i]+scale*g[i]  over the flat param blob,
  //    calling looksam_perturb_step (looksam.h:27-38). backup = a carved workspace
  //    region (sized `total`); grad stays the *first-pass* grad (read-only here).
  bar.sync();                          // perturbed weights visible to all CTAs
  bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);     // reset queue for the 2nd P1/P2 drain
  // 2. SECOND fwd+bwd+assembly into a SEPARATE grad_sam buffer:
  //    re-run dectc_forward_tile → dectc_backward_tile per tile (P1'), B1',
  //    then the P2' dW/bias/embed/lnvec assembly, writing grad_sam (NOT grad).

  // (P2' assembly … into grad_sam)
  // 3. set_direction: st.sam_dir[i] = grad_sam[i] - grad[i]  (looksam.h:52-59).
  // 4. RESTORE: p[i] = p_backup[i]  (looksam.h:42-48).
  bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);     // params restored; queue reset for P3

// P3: apply_optimizer<LookSAM> reads the now-populated st.sam_dir, blends
//     g_adj=(1-alpha)*g+alpha*sam_dir, runs AdamW (looksam.h:63-91) over `grad`.
```
